questions.q: What does the summary say telling a partial truth amounts to?
a: Still a form of dishonesty, through omitted details
A sensible way to protect someone's feelings
A necessary skill in professional settings
The same thing as complete honesty
questions.why: Lesson 1 argues that leaving out decisive details is not real honesty, just a cleaner conscience.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest you take charge of your life?
a: By being honest about what you find within
By blaming circumstances beyond your control
By changing jobs and moving to a new city
By following your family's advice closely
questions.why: Lesson 2 says only honesty about yourself lets you free your mind and take responsibility.

questions.q: What happens when you repress anger, according to the summary?
a: Frustration builds and damages your relationships
The feeling disappears after a few days
Others respect you more for staying calm
You become more honest over time
questions.why: Lesson 3 says hidden frustration builds up and can ruin the relationships you were protecting.

questions.q: What does the summary say about the persona people build?
a: Trouble with it can lead people to lie as a defence
It naturally fades as people grow older
It always reflects reality accurately
It should be protected by hiding the truth
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes lying as the survival mechanism people reach for when their persona is challenged.

questions.q: What does the summary recommend when something bothers you in a relationship?
a: Discuss it openly instead of keeping it inside
Wait until the other person notices
Write it down and never share it
Reduce contact until the feeling fades
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the best relationships are built on honesty and open communication.
